question: What is the most common immune-mediated toxicity of CD3-engaging bispecific antibodies in this review?
explanation: The review identifies cytokine-release syndrome as the most common immune-mediated toxicity of CD3-engaging bispecific antibodies [1].
sourceArticle: Safety and efficacy of bispecific antibodies in hematologic neoplasms: a systematic review

question: When do most cytokine-release events begin, and what grade are they?
explanation: Most cytokine-release events were grade 1–2 and developed within 1 to 2 days [1].
sourceArticle: Safety and efficacy of bispecific antibodies in hematologic neoplasms: a systematic review

question: The reported range of cytokine-release syndrome incidence across studies was:
explanation: Across studies, cytokine-release syndrome incidence ranged from 1.59% to 82.61% [1].
sourceArticle: Safety and efficacy of bispecific antibodies in hematologic neoplasms: a systematic review

question: What neurotoxicity figure does the review give for several blinatumomab studies?

options.A: Neurologic events in more than 50% of patients
options.C: Neurologic events only in solid tumours

correctAnswerText: Neurologic events in more than 50% of patients
explanation: Neurologic events were above 50% in several blinatumomab studies. Teclistamab and talquetamab also had reported neurotoxicity along with frequent cytokine release [1].
sourceArticle: Safety and efficacy of bispecific antibodies in hematologic neoplasms: a systematic review

question: How does the review describe bispecific evidence in Hodgkin and T-cell lymphoma at the time of writing?

options.A: Early-phase, limited efficacy, and no approvals yet
options.B: Standard first-line therapy with many approvals
options.D: Replacing CHOP with a labelled indication

correctAnswerText: Early-phase, limited efficacy, and no approvals yet
explanation: Hodgkin lymphoma and T-cell lymphoma programmes were described as early-phase, with limited efficacy and no approvals to date in the review [1].
sourceArticle: Safety and efficacy of bispecific antibodies in hematologic neoplasms: a systematic review
